title.narrative: Integrated multi-sector lifesaving humanitarian assistance for people affected by critical malnutrition needs in Guto Gida Woreda (East Wellega Zone)

description.narrative: ltpgtSwiss Church Aid (HEKS/EPER) and Fayyaa Integrated Development Organization (FIDO) are proposing an integrated multi-sector lifesaving intervention to support people affected by critical malnutrition in conflict-affected Guto Gida Woreda of East Wellega, Oromia Region. It is to be noted that HEKS/EPER and FIDO are among few organizations with strong operational presence in East Wellega. The intervention will have an integrated focus on two sectors: Agriculture and Health, with HEKS/EPER, and FIDO leading on one sector each, contributing their experience, resources, and staffing in a complementary manner. The intervention is based on a pre-project needs assessment (annexed) conducted in ltbrgtGuto Gida Woreda in June 2025. The proposed intervention, which is designed with input from communities, sector offices, and other humanitarian actors, will directly benefit 34,990 conflict-affected persons (17,495 F, 17,495 M). A strong focus will be on returnees (22,078 persons) and host community members (12,912 persons). A total of 4,289 persons with disability (11%) will benefit. ltbrgtViolent conflict led to severe human, asset and infrastructural damage, leaving the population in Guto Gida Woreda isolated, underserved and extremely vulnerable. In this scenario of high humanitarian needs, the two Project Partners, who have direct presence of staff and logistics, have consulted communities and local authorities to identify the prioritized sectors for intervention. As a result, Agriculture and Health were identified as high priority sectors. The project was designed strictly following the Ethiopia Priority Humanitarian Response and Critical Gaps document for February-April 2025 and Cross Cutting Directive.ltbrgtThe integrated Agriculture and Health response in Guto Gida Woreda aligns with respective Cluster Objectives and HRP 2025 priorities. Beneficiary selection will be fair, transparent and inclusive, and feedback and compliant mechanisms will be established. The agriculture component will support 18,505 people, including returnees, through seed distribution, poultry restocking, and sustainable farming training to restore livelihoods and improve food security. Emergency livestock support includes vouchers for treatment, veterinary drugs for four facilities, and three vaccination campaigns to protect productive assets. Health activities, benefitting 25,232 people, led by Mobile Health and Nutrition Teams (MHNTs), will provide essential services including outpatient care, immunization, and malnutrition screening, alongside health messaging and hygiene promotion. Disease surveillance will be strengthened via training, community-based early warning, and immunization campaigns, while damaged health facilities will be rehabilitated to restore local health systems.ltbrgtA Risk Management Plan has been developed for this project (annexed). The project was designed in coordination with relevant UN Clusters which provided their inputs and feedback. The local government is fully supportive of the proposed project (recognition certificate annexed). Due attention was given to complementarity with other ongoing interventions, including other projects funded by CERF/CBPF.ltbrgtlt/pgt
